_README: MEASURE these properties before the session and replace the placeholder
values below. mass_g with a kitchen scale, aperture_mm with a ruler or
calipers at the point where the hand actually closes. These numbers are
the ANCHOR MODALITY -- they are what the cross-modal model aligns EMG to,
and they are what unseen-object zero-shot generalisation is measured in.
Guessed values will silently degrade every downstream result.
'null' is the empty-hand pseudo-object used by every AIR trial. Its
aperture is the free-closure aperture: close your empty hand as if on the
cup and measure the gap between thumb pad and index pad. Do not set it to
zero -- the null object must sit at a real, measured point in the property

null.notes: PLACEHOLDER -- measure free-closure aperture for each subject.

cup.notes: PLACEHOLDER. Empty plastic/paper cup. Low EMG but genuinely loaded -- this is the object that breaks amplitude-only baselines.

bottle.notes: PLACEHOLDER. Full 500 ml bottle. High EMG, high load.

pen.notes: PLACEHOLDER. Light but a completely different synergy from the power grasps.

foam.notes: PLACEHOLDER. Compliant contact with no rigid arrest -- held out as the unseen object by default.

_held_out_note: Objects listed here are excluded from training and used only for the unseen-object zero-shot evaluation. Add more novel objects (stapler, apple, tape roll) here as you acquire them; they still need measured properties.
